questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Previous knowledge about the university, the country, and that a well known scientist in my field was there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not specifically easy, I fell like it could have been made clearer especially considering that everybody is doing the same thing. Also we had to go through undergraduate introduction which was unecessary.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Email´s with some introduction, a 3 day introduction course before start, but most of the 3 day introduction course was for undergraduates and irellevant for us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I feel like you could make it much clearer and focus on internation and transfer students more.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Tough and very very expensive. Start a few months before on facebook groups and try to find a room that is being subletted. NOT in oakland but stay in berkeley south or north and be aware of scammers. Also stay away from peoples park, there are violent homeless people we literally get a notification a few times a month due to violence or burglary that students have experienced by going by.

Or take a dorm at international house

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It allows you to hae more connection with american students, you can often get something better for cheaper than a dorm, and you have your own place. It is just a lot easier to find a palce where somebody is subletting a room than to find a completely new apartment. Also there is a lot of scammers online, so be aware when finding a room somewhere. 

Be aware of homeless people and peoples park.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most expensive rooms ever, and tough to find. Terrible housign situation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system is quite terrible and I got my final courses a few weeks before. Just stay calm, and wait until one or two weeks before deadline, before you cahnge your initial choices. Also you have to be aware of when the lectures for each coruse is planned, as you can not have two coruses which overlap at any time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find the coruse on the Cal dashboard, sign up to a course and either get on a waitlist or an error message. Then as the final deadline approaches you will get into the courses and hopefully all of them will be turned from waitlisted to enrolled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write proffesors or advisors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of them, even those that were very unlikely by writing to the professors

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be calm, do not mind being on the waitlist, and write proffesors or advisros if in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really enjoued it, but relies a lot on memorisation for biology.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were okay, nothing special. There was a lot to remember and fewer things to figure out. You are more than well prepared when you come form Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UC Berkeley they rely a lot on remembering and going to lectures, where at we at UCPH rely more on usign the knowledge to solve problems. Also the lab courses here are not the same standard, normally fewer proffesors at teachers for each student, and shorter easier days. Most have no knowledge in the Lab at all, so you will definetely excell or be bored in those classes. They do however have more specific courses which is a huge plus, and some of the proffesors are brilliant.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MCB: 149 human genome; 150 immunology; 150L Immunology laboratory;160 neurobiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of those I took, they give a nice overview of specialized courses we do not have on KU and gives you basic knowledge in neurobiology and immunology. if you are interested in that.

questions.answer: Go travel, rent a car with the other danish students

questions.answer: Go travel, rent a car with the other danish students

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, no problems at all

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk with them, go to gatherings etc. They are incredibly social

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All the homeless people

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly and open everybody were

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have a lot of money, talk and engage with people who are american, do not stress about all the midterms just read through and remmeber the slides and do show up!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find an american friend in a frat, have them help you get in to the nice parties

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Cultural experience and a chance to see everything from afar, new perspective on denmark and home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homeless people and expenses
